source_name: MNB – Készpénzfizetés jogszabályi környezete (legal framework of cash payment)
why_relevant: Central bank's own consolidated explanation of cash-acceptance rules, legal tender obligations and cash-handling decrees; the fastest authoritative map of which legal instruments govern cash at POS/ATM.

source_name: MNB – Jelentés a Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület éves tevékenységéről (Financial Arbitration Board annual report series)
why_relevant: Annual case statistics by product and dispute type; card, ATM, account and unauthorised-transaction case counts are an indirect but consistent indicator of card/ATM usage patterns and emerging fraud/service issues.

source_name: Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület – dedicated site
why_relevant: Case-handling portal of the financial arbitration body; publishes procedural statistics, decisions and thematic case summaries relevant to card/ATM disputes between consumers and banks.

source_name: MNB – Pénzügyi fogyasztóvédelmi (és piacfelügyeleti) jelentés
why_relevant: Annual consumer-protection report containing volumes and breakdowns of consumer complaints/petitions to the MNB, including payment-account, card and ATM-related complaint categories and identified consumer risks.

source_name: MNB – Pénzügyi panasz / fogyasztóvédelem consumer portal
why_relevant: Describes the complaint channels (institution → MNB → PBT → court, plus Kormányablak intake) and thus tells a collector where each complaint statistic originates and how the series are defined.

source_name: MNB – Pénzforgalmi ellenőrzés: kiemelt vizsgálati szempontok (payments supervision priorities)
source_subtype: supervisory framework page (gateway to enforcement decisions)
why_relevant: MNB acts as the national competent authority for the EU Interchange Fee Regulation and payment rules; its inspection priorities and sanction decisions reveal where interchange/surcharging/ATM-fee compliance is failing.

source_name: EUR-Lex – Regulation (EU) 2015/751 on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions
why_relevant: The binding interchange caps (0.2%/0.3%) applying directly in Hungary; the numeric anchor against which Hungarian scheme fees, MIF disclosures and merchant-cost analyses must be read. Hungarian language version available via EUR-Lex.

source_name: MNB Occasional Paper 96 – A bankközi jutalék szerepe a kártyás fizetési rendszerekben / The role of the interchange fee in card payment systems
why_relevant: Central-bank research establishing the analytical baseline and Hungarian-specific data on interchange economics; useful as a methodological reference and for historical fee levels pre-cap.

source_name: MNB – Költségvetési jelentés (fiscal/budget analysis report series)
why_relevant: MNB's analysis of the annual budget act discusses planned and realised revenue lines, including transaction-levy receipts — an independent cross-check on Ministry of Finance figures and on implied payment turnover.

source_name: Adózóna jogtár / tax-professional legal commentary (adozona.hu)
why_relevant: Practitioner commentary that flags each levy amendment quickly and explains scope changes (e.g. securities 2022, e-money 2025) in plain language — a fast early-warning layer over the gazette.

source_name: Big-4 / advisory Hungarian tax alerts on the transaction levy (Deloitte HU, RSM Hungary, Andersen HU)
why_relevant: Advisory alerts summarise levy scope expansions and their operational impact on banks, PSPs and e-money issuers — useful for interpreting how levy changes reshape pricing of card, ATM and transfer transactions.

source_name: Portfolio.hu / Economx / Index – Hungarian financial press coverage of payment legislation
why_relevant: Fastest signal that a payments-relevant act has appeared in Magyar Közlöny (e.g. doubling of free ATM withdrawal to HUF 300k from 2026-02-01, per-transaction minimum limits raised to HUF 150k from 2025-10-01), with the numeric thresholds and bank reactions; use as a pointer to the gazette text.

source_name: NKFH – Nemzeti Kereskedelmi és Fogyasztóvédelmi Hatóság (general consumer protection authority) and the general békéltető testület network
why_relevant: Enforces the general consumer-protection act — including the new obligation to offer cash payment at merchants — so its inspection campaigns and sanctions are the observable measure of cash-acceptance compliance at POS.

source_name: Pénzügyi Navigátor Tanácsadó Irodahálózat (MNB consumer advisory network)
why_relevant: MNB-affiliated advisory network whose complaint intake and thematic guidance surface recurring card, ATM and account-fee problems ahead of formal statistics.

source_name: Arcanum Digitheca – Magyar Közlöny 1945–2019 digital archive
why_relevant: Full-text searchable historical gazette archive for reconstructing the long-run legislative history of cash, levy and payment rules beyond what the current portal exposes.

source_name: Portfolio.hu Rendezvények (conference portal, Financial IT / Hitelezés / Future of Finance)
why_relevant: Hungary's dominant business-conference organiser for finance; agendas and speaker lists for Financial IT, Future of Finance, Hitelezés, Követeléskezelési trendek name the MNB payments directors, bank COOs and vendor executives who present transaction volumes and roadmaps months before official statistics. Portfolio also publishes article write-ups quoting the numbers shown on stage.

source_name: TechShow X (merged PayTechShow + BankTechShow), Budapest
why_relevant: The Hungarian payments-and-banking-tech community's flagship two-day event; agenda tracks reportedly cover cards, instant payments/AFR, POS and softPOS, acquiring, wallets, ISO 20022 and the EU Instant Payments Regulation. Agenda + sponsor/exhibitor list is effectively a supplier map of who sells POS/ATM/switching into Hungary.

source_name: Mastercard – Év Bankja (Bank of the Year) award programme
why_relevant: Twenty-year-old national banking award with segment/category structure (daily banking, innovation, beyond banking, AI-based innovation of the year, etc.). Submissions and jury write-ups routinely disclose product volumes, user counts and roadmap claims banks do not publish elsewhere; the winner list is a direct read on which institutions are pushing payment innovation.

source_name: MNB Fizetési Rendszer Fórum (Payment System Forum / Payment System Council)
why_relevant: Central-bank-chaired standing forum (three-tier structure, Fizetési Rendszer Tanács at the top) where the market agrees instant-payment, qvik and fraud-prevention roadmaps. Meeting materials/communiqués are the earliest official signal of scheme changes and mandated go-live dates that later show up in statistics.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség (Hungarian Banking Association) news & press releases
why_relevant: Industry body whose news and press-release stream announces sector positions, working groups, conferences and joint bank initiatives (cash access, instant payments, fraud). Useful for spotting coordinated industry moves and for identifying named committee experts as human sources.

source_name: Profession.hu job board — POS / acquiring / card / ATM roles
why_relevant: Hungary's largest job board. Vacancy text for POS-terminal product managers, acquiring specialists, ATM field-service and instant-payment/AFR engineers reveals which bank or PSP is building what, on which platform, and at what scale — typically 6-18 months ahead of any published statistic. A result set explicitly included a role leading product strategy and roadmap for mobile and POS terminal solutions.

source_name: Indeed Hungary (hu.indeed.com) — payments/banking vacancies
why_relevant: Second aggregator giving coverage of employers that do not post to Profession, including vendors, processors and ATM operators. Cross-board deduplication improves recall of hiring signals.

source_name: Jooble Hungary — aggregated vacancy feed
why_relevant: Meta-aggregator that surfaces postings from smaller HU boards and corporate career sites; useful as a recall net for niche acquiring/ATM/terminal roles missed by the big two.

source_name: GIRO Zrt. corporate site + career portal (giro.karrierportal.hu)
why_relevant: Operator of the HU clearing/instant-payment infrastructure (AFR) and of qvik. Its news and — critically — its own career portal expose the build agenda: qvik physical/POS rollout, the Központi Visszaélésszűrő Rendszer (KVR) fraud-screening system with Magyar Telekom, and volume ambitions (stated plan of 40-50 million transactions/month by 2026-2027, two sub-aggregators: OTP Mobile and Raiffeisen).

source_name: Euronet Magyarország ATM press releases and newsroom
why_relevant: Largest independent (non-bank) ATM deployer in Hungary — publicly described as operating roughly 600 ATMs, most dual-currency. Its press releases and blog announce network changes, bank partnerships (e.g. the MagNet fee-parity arrangement) and fee moves — leading indicators for cash-usage and ATM-estate statistics that MNB publishes with a long lag.

source_name: TED / EU public procurement notices for Hungarian bank-card acceptance and POS services
why_relevant: Hungarian public bodies must tender card-acceptance and POS-terminal services; a notice surfaced in search concerned bankkártyaelfogadás / POS terminal services in Budapest. Notices and award results disclose terminal counts, transaction volumes, MSC pricing and the winning acquirer — hard quantitative signal not otherwise public.

source_name: Hiventures — Hungarian state venture capital fund manager
why_relevant: Largest HU state VC; reported in 2026 to have launched a HUF 17bn early-stage programme with tickets up to EUR 300k. Its portfolio and announcement pages are the most systematic public list of funded Hungarian fintech/payment startups, i.e. the future competitive set.
